name: ESP-12F(ESP8266MOD)
title: ESP-12F: 2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n Wi-Fi module on the ESP8266, PCB antenna, 32 Mbit flash
summary: A 24 × 16 × 3 mm surface-mount Wi-Fi module with castellated pads (SMD22) built around the ESP8266EX, with 32 Mbit of SPI flash, a 26 MHz crystal and a printed antenna. The ESP8266's 32-bit core at 80 or 160 MHz can run the application or act as a Wi-Fi adapter for a host. It runs from 3.0 to 3.6 V, draws about 71 mA average and 500 mA peak in continuous transmit and 20 µA in deep sleep, and works from -20 to 85 °C. Sixteen pads are usable: supply, reset, enable, the ADC, UART0 and nine GPIO; six more on the bottom edge belong to the flash.

pins.name: RST
pins.function: Reset; a low level resets the module.

pins.name: ADC
pins.function: Input of the ESP8266's ADC. Range 0 to 1 V, read as a value from 0 to 1024.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Chip enable; high runs the chip. Called CH_PD in the boot-mode table.

pins.name: IO16
pins.function: GPIO16. Wired to RST, it wakes the module from deep sleep.

pins.name: IO15
pins.function: GPIO15; MTDO; HSPICS; UART0_RTS. Low at boot for both UART download and flash boot.

pins.name: IO0
pins.function: GPIO0; HSPI_MISO; I2SI_DATA. Low at boot selects UART download; high selects running from flash.

notes: Sixteen usable pins: 1 to 8 run down one long side from RST, at the antenna end, to VCC; 9 to 16 run back up the other side from GND to TXD.

pins.name: GPIO16
pins.function: GPIO16, deep-sleep wake when tied to RST.

pins.name: CS0
pins.function: Internal SPI flash chip select (SD_CMD); not for use.

pins.name: MISO
pins.function: Internal SPI flash DO/IO1 (SD_D0); not for use.

pins.name: GPIO9
pins.function: Internal SPI flash HOLD/IO3 (SD_D2); not for use.

pins.name: GPIO10
pins.function: Internal SPI flash WP/IO2 (SD_D3); not for use.

pins.name: MOSI
pins.function: Internal SPI flash DI/IO0 (SD_D1); not for use.

pins.name: SCLK
pins.function: Internal SPI flash clock (SD_CLK); not for use.

notes: Pads 1 to 8 run down one long side from RST, at the antenna end, to VCC; 9 to 14 cross the short edge opposite the antenna; 15 to 22 run back up the other long side from GND to TXD0.

tables.title: Power consumption
tables.conditions: 3.3 V supply through a regulator, 25 °C ambient; transmit figures at 50% duty cycle in continuous transmission
notes: (1) Modem sleep keeps the CPU running (for PWM or I2S, say) and switches off the Wi-Fi modem between beacons while the association to the access point holds. With DTIM3, sleeping 300 ms and waking 3 ms for each beacon, the average is about 20 mA.
(2) Light sleep switches off the CPU as well as the modem while the association holds. With the same DTIM3 pattern of 300 ms asleep and 3 ms awake, the average is about 2 mA.

(3) Deep sleep drops the Wi-Fi association; it suits a device that reports rarely, such as a sensor read every 100 s. Sleeping 300 s and then taking about 0.3 to 1 s to rejoin the access point averages well under 1 mA. The 20 µA figure was measured at 2.5 V.

circuits.title: Application circuit
circuits.description: The least the module needs to boot from its flash and talk over UART0. A 3.3 V rail of 500 mA or more, recommended to come from a DC-DC or LDO regulator of its own, feeds VCC with 10 µF and 100 nF to ground. RST and EN are each pulled up to 3.3 V through 10 kΩ, so the chip is enabled and out of reset. GPIO0 is pulled up and GPIO15 pulled down through 10 kΩ, which selects running from flash. TXD0 and RXD0 go to the host's receive and transmit lines. The six flash pins on the bottom edge are left unconnected.
notes: Pin numbers are those of the 22-pad list: 1 to 8 from RST to VCC, 9 to 14 the flash pads, 15 to 22 from GND to TXD0.

operation.text: An ESP8266EX SoC with a 26 MHz ±10 ppm crystal and a W25Q32 SPI flash wired to its SD_CMD, SD_CLK, SD_D0 to SD_D3 lines. The supply has 10 µF and 0.1 µF on board. The radio pin feeds the PCB antenna (WIFI_ANT, 50 Ω) through a 5.6 pF series capacitor, with two shunt inductor positions left unfitted. The chip's EXT_RSTB is pulled up to 3.3 V by 12 kΩ, held by 1 µF to ground, and reaches the RST pad through 470 Ω. RES12K has 12 kΩ to ground.

The SoC runs a Tensilica L106 32-bit core at 80 MHz or 160 MHz with an RTOS, and integrates the Wi-Fi MAC, baseband, RF, power amplifier and LNA. It can run the user's application itself, booting from the external flash, or serve another microcontroller as a network adapter over SPI, SDIO, I2C or UART. A cache sits in front of the flash.

IEEE 802.11 b/g/n in station, access-point or both modes together, with an lwIP TCP/IP stack, Smart Config and AirKiss provisioning, over-the-air firmware update and AT-command firmware. Development is supported on Windows and Linux.
UART up to 4 Mbps, GPIO, I2C, PWM and a 10-bit ADC. Nine I/O ports are brought out.
With EN and RST high, GPIO15 low and GPIO2 and TXD0 high, GPIO0 picks the boot: low enters UART download, high runs the program in flash. GPIO15 high selects SDIO/SPI boot.
GPIO16 connected to RST lets the module wake itself from deep sleep.
The 3.3 V supply should come from a DC-DC or LDO regulator of its own, rated 500 mA or more. Peak current in transmit is 500 mA.
The six pads on the bottom edge (CS0, MISO, GPIO9, GPIO10, MOSI, SCLK) carry the internal flash bus and are not available to the user.
The PCB antenna takes the top 6.2 mm of the module's length, the end away from the bottom-edge pads.
Supplied in trays or on reels.
